items.title: Controlled form
items.body:
const [form, setForm] = useState({ email: "", password: "" });

const update = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) =>
  setForm((f) => ({ ...f, [e.target.name]: e.target.value }));

<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  <input name="email" value={form.email} onChange={update} />
  <input name="password" type="password" value={form.password} onChange={update} />
</form>
items.description: Single state object for several inputs.

Required<User>                // all required
Pick<User, "id" | "name">     // only these keys

items.title: type vs interface
items.body:
interface User { id: number; name: string }            // objects; can be extended/merged
type Status = "idle" | "loading" | "error";             // unions, tuples, primitives
type Admin = User & { permissions: string[] };           // intersections
Use interface for public object shapes, type for everything else.
items.description: Rule of thumb for choosing.

items.title: React Router basics
items.body:
import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Link, useParams } from "react-router-dom";

<BrowserRouter>
  <nav><Link to="/">Home</Link></nav>
  <Routes>
    <Route path="/" element={<Home />} />
    <Route path="/users/:id" element={<User />} />
    <Route path="*" element={<NotFound />} />
  </Routes>
</BrowserRouter>

const { id } = useParams<{ id: string }>();
items.description: Routes with a param (react-router-dom v6/v7 API).
